record.original_question: For virtual 3-manifolds defined from framed virtual link diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves, do virtual Kirby equivalence and classical Kirby equivalence coincide on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed classical links; what is the correct geometric-topology interpretation of a virtual 3-manifold; and does the alternative construction by surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization produce the same theory?

evidence.quote: There is a theory of virtual 3-manifolds constructed as formal equivalence classes of virtual diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves, see [18]. From this point of view, there are two equivalences for ordinary 3-manifolds: homeomorphisms and virtual equivalence. Do these equivalences coincide?

What is a virtual 3-manifold? That is, give an interpretation of these equivalence classes in the domain of geometric topology. Construct another theory of virtual 3-manifolds by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces Sg × R considered up to stabilization. Will this theory coincide to that proposed by Kauffman and Dye [18]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (over/under information) or virtual crossings (small circles indicating that the two strands are not actually linked in the plane). Two virtual link diagrams are considered equivalent if they are related by a finite sequence of the classical Reidemeister moves, the virtual Reidemeister moves, and the mixed (semi-virtual) detour move. A framed virtual link diagram carries an integer framing on each component.

There is a notion of generalized Kirby moves on framed virtual link diagrams: these consist of (i) the classical Kirby moves (handle slide and stabilization/destabilization by an unknot with framing ±1) and (ii) the virtual Reidemeister and detour moves applied to framed diagrams. Define a virtual 3-manifold to be an equivalence class of framed virtual link diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves. Two framed virtual links are called virtually Kirby equivalent if they represent the same virtual 3-manifold; two framed classical links are classically Kirby equivalent if they are related by classical Kirby moves alone.

Alternatively, given a closed oriented surface S_g of genus g, consider framed links in the thickening S_g × R. Surgery along such a link produces a closed oriented 3-manifold. Declare two such surgery presentations equivalent if they are related by classical Kirby moves performed within some thickening, together with stabilizations of the ambient surface (replacing S_g × R by S_{g+1} × R by attaching a 1-handle to the surface and extending the link trivially across it). Call the resulting equivalence classes stabilized thickened-surface 3-manifolds.

Problems.
(a) For two framed classical link diagrams L_1, L_2 (i.e. virtual link diagrams without virtual crossings), prove or disprove that L_1 and L_2 are virtually Kirby equivalent if and only if they are classically Kirby equivalent. Equivalently, decide whether the natural map from classical Kirby equivalence classes of framed classical links to virtual Kirby equivalence classes of framed virtual links is injective, so that ordinary 3-manifolds are not collapsed under the virtual equivalence.

(b) Give an intrinsic geometric-topology interpretation of a virtual 3-manifold: describe a category of geometric objects (e.g., 3-manifolds equipped with extra structure, or equivalence classes of pairs (Y, L) involving thickened surfaces and links) whose isomorphism classes are in natural bijection with virtual Kirby equivalence classes of framed virtual link diagrams.

(c) Show whether the theory of stabilized thickened-surface 3-manifolds defined above coincides with the theory of virtual 3-manifolds defined via generalized Kirby moves on framed virtual link diagrams; that is, construct a natural bijection between the two sets of equivalence classes, or exhibit explicit examples distinguishing them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as a known unsolved question in the area of virtual knot theory and virtual 3-manifolds, restated in several surveys of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory. No published proof of (a), (b), or (c) was found in the search, and the question is still listed among open problems in the field.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Virtual Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey paper compiling unsolved problems in virtual knot theory, including virtual 3-manifold questions.
status_evidence.claim: The questions about virtual 3-manifolds and their relationship to ordinary 3-manifolds and to thickened-surface constructions are listed among unsolved problems.

status_evidence.title: Virtual knot - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Virtual knots are knots in thickened surfaces taken up to homeomorphism and handle stabilization.
status_evidence.claim: Virtual knot theory uses both diagrammatic and thickened-surface models, but the equivalence of the resulting virtual 3-manifold theories is not established.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Knot Diagrams and the Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariant (Dye, Kauffman)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops a theory of virtual 3-manifolds via generalized Kirby moves on framed virtual link diagrams.
status_evidence.claim: The diagrammatic theory of virtual 3-manifolds referenced in the problem is the one developed by Dye and Kauffman.
